pr_title: JsonConsoleFormatter: keep escaped line breaks for Exceptions #83726
pr_body:
Fixes #83726

Linebreaks of Exceptions no longer get removed in JsonConsoleFormatter, but instead get escaped by `Utf8JsonWriter`, so original format can be restored by log viewer.

issue_context.title: JsonConsoleFormatter: (escaped) line breaks of exception stacktraces should be kept
issue_context.body:
### Description

JsonConsoleFormatter is a great option for logging in cloud infrastructure where logs can be picked up from stdout.

For this JsonConsoleFormatter is probably mostly used with the FormatterOptions SingleLine=true, JsonWriterOptions.Indented=false:

```
"Console": {
  "FormatterName": "json",
  "FormatterOptions": {
    "SingleLine": true,
    "IncludeScopes": true,
    "TimestampFormat": "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffzzz"
  }
}
```

This produces an output similar to the one described in 'Actual behaviour'.

The downside of this is, in case of an Exception, that line breaks for serialized `Exception`'s get stripped (manually, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c1acb35ce2b90f241ccdf3ead79544516c673e5f/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console/src/JsonConsoleFormatter.cs#L59). For comparison, this is not the case for the `Message` part of the logged Json. There line breaks are kept in an escaped manner.

These escaped line breaks can then get picked up again and formatted properly in the log viewer of your desire. This is not possible for Exceptions, their serialized form gets broken.

I would like to see escaped line breaks in the serialized Exception string too, as we do for the Message, in the logged Json. Is there any reason this is not the case? Does this need to be backwards compatible? Or could it be simply changed in the line referenced above?

Nothing should change for the `JsonWriterOptions.Indented` mode, there everything is formatted properly.

### Reproduction Steps

Log an exception with `JsonConsoleFormatter` in `SingleLine` mode:

```
"Console": {
  "FormatterName": "json",
  "FormatterOptions": {
    "SingleLine": true,
    "IncludeScopes": true,
    "TimestampFormat": "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffzzz"
  }
}
```

```
logger.LogError(e, "{Message}", e.Message);
```

### Expected behavior

```

### Regression?

Looks like it was always like this.

### Known Workarounds

It should be configuration independent.

> any idea why we are explicitly replacing line breaks for exception messages? The formatted JSON shouldn't be affected by their presence.

I don't know the reason behind that but looks to me escaping the line break instead of stripping it is the correct thing to do.

review_comments: Don't we need to escape the new lines before writing it?
Ah, I see it get escaped by `Utf8JsonWriter`. So, this will be fine then. We need to have an E2E test for the case to ensure the newlines are escaped.

Exactly, `Utf8JsonWriter` takes care of escaping already, so the change is "trivial".
